_why: El suelo de version de los modulos cuyas operaciones pide esta plantilla. tests/flow_templates.test.py resuelve los nombres contra los checkouts VECINOS del workspace, y un checkout viejo convierte un rojo en un verde (whatsapp_inbox#52). Cada familia declara el suyo y no se comparte: la bateria busca el fichero por el nombre de la familia, y una familia sin suelo propio es una familia que se valida contra lo que la maquina tenga a mano. Viaja ademas al hub desde hub#1611: `flow_template_floor_is_met` decide con el si la receta se OFRECE.
_appointments: 1.1.77 desde whatsapp_inbox#146, y NO lo pide esta receta sino su ACOMPANANTE: la tarjeta de citas enciende tambien `appointment-confirmed-to-whatsapp`, cuyo aviso nombra el dia y la hora con dos columnas que `appointments.appointments.get` solo contesta desde el release 1.1.77 (ver su requires.json). `flow_template_floor_is_met` (hub#1611) decide POR FAMILIA si una receta se ofrece, asi que con esta en 1.1.76 un hub en 1.1.76 exacto aceptaria la tarjeta y rechazaria el aviso: «Activo» en pantalla y la clienta sin mensaje. Lo vigila «a companion never demands a NEWER neighbour than the card that carries it» en `ui/lib/whatsapp-uses.test.ts`. Lo que sigue es por que el suelo PROPIO de esta receta es 1.1.76. Las tres operaciones de disponibilidad que el paso `book_appointment` necesita NO aterrizaron a la vez: `appointments.availability.day_opening` se publica en 1.1.63 (appointments#105), `.check` pasa a command en 1.1.67 (appointments#122) y `.slots` en 1.1.68 (appointments#127). El suelo, sin embargo, ya no lo fija la disponibilidad sino la ANULACION: desde whatsapp_inbox#82 la plantilla manda `customer_id` en `appointments.appointments.cancel`, y ese campo lo estrena appointments 1.1.72 (appointments#140, PR #141). Por debajo de esa version el schema del command es `additionalProperties: false` SIN `customer_id`, asi que la anulacion no se degrada: se rechaza entera con `invalid_payload`. 1.1.72 es un suelo DURO, no una holgura — el numero que no se puede cruzar es exactamente ese. Y desde whatsapp_inbox#105 el suelo lo fija MOVER, un escalon mas arriba: la plantilla manda `channel` + `customer_id` en `appointments.appointments.reschedule`, y ese par lo estrena appointments 1.1.73 (appointments#142, PR #144). Medido, no supuesto: `channel` entra en el commit 408c356, POSTERIOR al `chore(release): v1.1.72` (825a95d), y `git show 825a95d:schemas/appointment_reschedule.json | grep -c channel` da 0. Ese schema tambien es `additionalProperties: false`, asi que contra 1.1.72 el cambio de hora no se degrada: se rechaza entero con `invalid_payload`. 1.1.73 es un suelo DURO. (Anular por WhatsApp, whatsapp_inbox#61, no lo subia: `appointments.appointments.list_for_customer` viene de appointments#46 y el campo `channel` aterrizo en 1.1.32, muy por debajo.) Y desde whatsapp_inbox#137 el suelo lo fija EL INTERRUPTOR de la tarjeta, un escalon mas arriba todavia: la tarjeta pinta «se confirman solas / las reviso yo» en cuanto la receta esta corriendo, y esa decision se escribe con el command estrecho `appointments.settings.set_auto_confirm_online`, que NO existia cuando se fijo el 1.1.73. Medido sobre los arboles publicados, no sobre el commit: `648ac35` (appointments#150) anade el command con el manifest todavia en una version anterior, y como el zip `modules/appointments/v<X>.zip` se sube CREATE-ONLY, el primer release que lo LLEVA es `52588bf` = `chore(release): v1.1.76` — los arboles de 1.1.73, 1.1.74 y 1.1.75 no lo declaran (comprobado uno a uno). En la horquilla [1.1.73, 1.1.76) la receta se ofrecia, se activaba y funcionaba, y el interruptor de debajo rechazaba todos los cambios con `ui.useAppointmentsPolicyError`. 1.1.76 es un suelo DURO por la misma razon que los de arriba: no se degrada, se rechaza. Lo vigila la bateria «the one decision this screen owns exists at the floor its recipe declares» de `ui/lib/whatsapp-uses.test.ts`, que lee el manifest del arbol publicado COMO el suelo y no el de `origin/main`.
_customers: The steps that find the customer by the number she writes from (`find_customer`, `resolve_customer`) read `customers.by_phone`, which compares NUMBERS rather than text (whatsapp_inbox#165): `customers.list` filtered `phone` with a LIKE over the raw column, so `34600111222` never found a card typed `600 111 222` and the recipe created a second card for a customer on file. `customers.by_phone` ships in customers 2.3.45 (customers#79, PR merged as 01af8f5 with the manifest still at 2.3.44, so the first zip that carries it is 2.3.45). Below that floor the read does not exist: the step fails on every message and nobody gets an answer. 2.3.45 is a HARD floor for the read to exist. And since whatsapp_inbox#202 the floor is 2.3.47: the step keeps the FIRST row `customers.by_phone` answers, and until customers#81 (PR merged as 5a897f9, first zip `120185f` = `chore(release): v2.3.47`) the query let ANY 1-3 digit country prefix through, so a French `33 600 111 222` writing to a Spanish salon came back as the local card `600 111 222` and was booked on it. Since 2.3.47 it reads the business's country from the core's `hub_settings.country_code` and only accepts that prefix. Measured on the published trees: the SQL of `f6b0a35` (v2.3.46) mentions neither `hub_settings` nor `country_code`. Below the floor the recipe does not fail, it books on a stranger's card, which is worse. Guarded by `home_country_match_problems` in tests/flow_templates.test.py, which reads that SQL at the declared floor; module.json `depends_on` carries the same 2.3.47.
_services: The `book_appointment` step hands its assistant `services.services.list` as a TOOL, to pick the service and read its `duration_minutes` (whatsapp_inbox#197). A tool is an operation the hub runs for the recipe exactly like a step is, so without a floor the recipe was offered next to ANY copy of Services, including one where the read does not exist: the assistant fails at its first question and the customer is left without her appointment. Measured on the published trees, not assumed: the first tree of ERPlora/services (`da2ceed`, the extraction, manifest 1.1.7) already declares `services.services.list` with its `ai` block, and its `queries/services_list.sql` already answers `duration_minutes`. 1.1.7 is the lowest version this repo ever declared, so the floor excludes nothing that ships the read and still makes a hub WITHOUT Services (or with it paused) not be offered the recipe.
_staff: The same step hands its assistant `staff.members.list` and `staff.schedules.list_for_member`, to pick a professional who really works at that hour (whatsapp_inbox#197). Measured the same way: the first tree of ERPlora/staff (`7e88078`, the extraction, manifest 2.0.4) already declares both reads with their `ai` blocks. 2.0.4 is the lowest version the repo ever declared; what the floor buys is that a hub without Staff, or with it paused, is no longer offered a recipe whose assistant cannot choose anybody.
